issue.title: sase-core-rs floor is 0.24.0 but observed_since bead-search indexing shipped in 0.24.1
issue.description: pyproject.toml declares sase-core-rs>=0.24.0,<0.25.0 and uv.lock resolves 0.24.0, but epic sase-ix's search indexing landed in sase-core commit 4f09d2774 ('feat(beads): search observed_since corroboration evidence'), which is first contained in tag v0.24.1 (verified today: 'git tag --contains 4f09d2774' -> v0.24.1, v0.24.2, v0.24.3, v0.24.4). IMPACT: any environment that resolves sase-core-rs from PyPI rather than building from a linked sase-core checkout -- notably a fresh workspace with no linked core -- cannot 'sase bead search' an observed_since timestamp, so post-close +1 corroboration that 'sase bead show' and 'sase bead list --status closed' both render is invisible to search. tests/test_bead/test_plus_one_presentation.py::test_post_close_plus_one_badge_marker_search_and_json_agree is the node that exposes it. sase-ix.5.land diagnosed this and declined to file a task on the assumption that tools/ratchet_core_window would raise the floor automatically once 0.24.1 published; 0.24.4 is now out and the floor is still 0.24.0, so the ratchet did not run. SCOPE: raise the pyproject floor past 4f09d2774, regenerate uv.lock, and check why ratchet_core_window did not fire -- this is the fifth instance of the same stale-floor pattern (sase-d7, sase-h0, sase-hz, sase-ic).

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-j6 — sase-j6 tracks the same failing node (test_post_close_plus_one_badge_marker_search_and_json_agree) as a full-parallel-lane flake. This bead is the separate deterministic cause for PyPI-resolved environments; fixing the floor may or may not clear sase-j6's parallel-lane signature.

RELATED: sase-d7, sase-h0, sase-hz, sase-ic — four earlier closed instances of the identical stale-core-floor pattern. If tools/ratchet_core_window is meant to prevent recurrence, its failure to fire here is the more valuable half of this fix.
